# Video References and External Demonstrations

**IMPORTANT:** The videos linked below are **EXTERNAL REFERENCES**. They are not generated by this project. They are provided here to demonstrate the visual concepts, driver behaviors, and computer vision techniques that this project implements.

## 1. Drowsiness Detection Concepts
**Title:** Real-time Eye Blink Detection (EAR Algorithm Demo)
- **Source:** PyImageSearch / Adrian Rosebrock (YouTube/Blog)
- **URL:** [PyImageSearch: Eye Blink Detection](https://pyimagesearch.com/2017/04/24/eye-blink-detection-opencv-python-dlib/)
- **What it demonstrates:** Visualizes how the EAR scalar value drops to zero during a blink, and how prolonged closure indicates drowsiness.
- **Relationship:** Task 1 of our project implements a similar EAR temporal tracking mechanism using MediaPipe rather than Dlib.

## 2. Distraction and Head Pose Concepts
**Title:** MediaPipe Face Mesh Head Pose Estimation
- **Source:** MediaPipe Community Demos
- **URL:** [MediaPipe Face Mesh](https://google.github.io/mediapipe/solutions/face_mesh.html)
- **What it demonstrates:** Shows how 3D landmarks react to a user looking away from the camera (Yaw/Pitch deviations).
- **Relationship:** Task 2 uses these exact 3D spatial properties to trigger distraction alerts when the driver looks away from the road for >2 seconds.

## 3. Driver Identification
**Title:** OpenCV Face Recognition using SFace
- **Source:** OpenCV Zoo Official Demos
- **URL:** [OpenCV Zoo GitHub](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_zoo/tree/main/models/face_recognition_sface)
- **What it demonstrates:** Real-time extraction of embeddings and cosine distance comparison between faces.
- **Relationship:** Task 3 implements this exact model pipeline, augmented with a temporal confidence filter to stabilize identification during driving.
